title: Outlook desktop: Create PDF from email that keeps the sensitivity label
summary: Hold: the mandatory-labelling path starts inside a policy without explaining how to reach it, and its automation is incorrectly reported as undocumented. The Office policy row also gives a Group Policy navigation path for Cloud Policy, which uses a different interface. The roadmap facts and both registry values are supported.

claims.claim: Mandatory labelling blocks Print to PDF for labelled content in Outlook Desktop.
claims.quote: Outlook Desktop blocks printing to PDF if Mandatory Labeling is enabled. This change is in all M365 channels beginning in January 2024.

claims.claim: The 2024 support page says Outlook Desktop did not support exporting files to PDF.
claims.quote: This error can be misleading since Outlook Desktop does not support exporting files to PDF.

claims.claim: Word, Excel and PowerPoint for Windows support exporting to PDF with the sensitivity label.
claims.quote: Office for Windows: Word, Excel, and PowerPoint support the following methods to convert an Office document into a PDF document: ... File > Export > PDF ... When the PDF is created, it inherits the label with any content markings.

claims.claim: PDFs created through the documented Word, Excel and PowerPoint conversion methods inherit content markings.
claims.quote: When the PDF is created, it inherits the label with any content markings.

claims.quote: Outlook doesn't currently support PDF attachments inheriting encryption from a labeled message.

claims.claim: Encrypted PDFs produced by the documented Office conversion methods can be opened with Microsoft Edge on Windows or Mac.
claims.quote: For Windows, if the label applied encryption, that encryption is also inherited. Encrypted PDFs can be opened with Microsoft Edge on Windows or Mac.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Print to PDF removes the sensitivity label.
claims.quote: Because this option removes the sensitivity label, this option won't be available to users if you're using mandatory labeling.

claims.claim: Print to PDF loses label encryption when encryption was applied.
claims.quote: If users select this option, they are warned that the document or email will lose the protection of the label, and encryption (if applied), and must confirm to continue.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[2].governs; controls[2].note; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The Outlook-specific registry workaround applies only to Outlook Desktop and allows Print to PDF without preserving the label or encryption.
claims.quote: The Outlook Team implemented a new registry key that only applies to Outlook Desktop. It enables printing to PDF without preserving the label or encryption.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Label policy configuration > Policy settings > Require users to apply a label to their email or documents is a complete route from the portal navigation.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies. ... To edit an existing label policy, select it, and then select the Edit Policy button from the flyout pane.
claims.fix: Keep the surface Microsoft Purview portal; replace the path with 'Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > policy > Edit Policy > Policy settings > Require users to apply a label to their email or documents'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels for the route into the policy and retain https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/sensitivity-labels-office-apps for the setting. Remove the duplicate portal name and the non-navigation step 'Label policy configuration'.

claims.claim: No automation is documented for the mandatory-labelling control.
claims.quote: DisableMandatoryInOutlook: Outlook apps that support this setting exempt Outlook messages from mandatory labeling. Example: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity Global -AdvancedSettings @{DisableMandatoryInOutlook="True"}
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].api null with kind 'powershell', call 'Set-LabelPolicy -Identity <policy> -AdvancedSettings @{DisableMandatoryInOutlook="True"}', and docs https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/set-labelpolicy. Add to the note: 'This call exempts Outlook messages from mandatory labelling in Outlook apps that support the setting; it does not configure mandatory labelling for documents.'

claims.claim: Mandatory labelling is set per label policy, with a separate email checkbox that can be cleared in supported Outlook apps.
claims.quote: When the Outlook app supports turning off mandatory labeling: ... Select Require users to apply a label to their email or documents. Then select Next > Next and clear the checkbox Require users to apply a label to their emails.

claims.claim: The User Configuration/Administrative Templates/Microsoft Office 2016/Microsoft Save As PDF and Save As XPS add-ins path works in Group Policy or Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. ... On the Configure Settings page, select the policies that you want to include in the policy configuration. You can search for the policy by name, or you can create a custom filter.
claims.fix: Narrow controls[1].ui.surface to 'Group Policy' and retain the existing path and Office-apps docs URL. Add to the note: 'Configure Use the Sensitivity feature in Office to apply sensitivity labels to PDFs as Disabled.' The cited Office-apps page documents that exact Group Policy location; do not present it as Cloud Policy navigation.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: HKCU\software\policies\microsoft\office\16.0\common\fixedformat disablepdfprotection (DWORD) = 1 disables PDF label handling for Print to PDF and export in Office applications.
claims.quote: The registry key disables saving with labels for both the Print to PDF as well as the export option in the Office applications. ... HKEY_CURRENT_USER\software\policies\microsoft\office\16.0\common\fixedformat DWORD: disablepdfprotection Value: 1

claims.claim: The Outlook workaround is HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Office\16.0\Outlook\Preferences disablepdfprotectioninoutlook (DWORD) = 1.
claims.quote: Path: HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Office\16.0\Outlook\Preferences Name: disablepdfprotectioninoutlook (dword32) Value: 1

claims.claim: No admin UI setting is documented for the Outlook-specific printing workaround.
claims.quote: Searched: "disablepdfprotectioninoutlook" Group Policy Cloud Policy; "disablepdfprotectioninoutlook". Read search results and the Print to PDF support page, which documents a registry value but no UI control for it.
